Simple Roleplay.prompt:

Everyday Situations.prompt: You have enough money to fix ONE thing in your apartment this month. Choose what to fix and explain why.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Choose only one thing to fix.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Your internet company offers two plans: one cheaper but slower, one faster but more expensive. Which do you choose for your household, and why?
Everyday Situations.constraint: Give at least one reason based on cost and one based on speed.

Everyday Situations.prompt: A friend's car needs a repair that will take either one day (expensive) or one week (cheaper). They ask what you'd do. Recommend an option and explain your reasoning.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Recommend only one option, based on their situation, not yours.

Everyday Situations.prompt: A friend wants to borrow money from you until next month. Decide how you'll respond and explain your reasoning.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Your answer must address both the friendship and the money.

Everyday Situations.prompt: You're choosing between two apartments: one with a shorter commute but higher rent, one with a longer commute but lower rent. Make your decision and justify it.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Mention at least one trade-off you're accepting.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Your roommate is worried about a higher-than-expected energy bill and asks what you think you should both do. Recommend a solution and explain why.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Recommend one specific action, not a list of possibilities.

Everyday Situations.prompt: You're planning meals for the week on a limited budget. Decide your approach and explain why it works.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Mention at least two meals and one cost-saving decision.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Your child's school trip costs more than you planned to spend this month, but your child really wants to go. Find a compromise between the cost and their wishes, and explain your reasoning.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Your compromise must involve a real trade-off, not a simple yes or no.

Everyday Situations.prompt: You have two days off this week but a long list of errands. Decide how to use the time and explain your priorities.
Everyday Situations.constraint: You must leave at least one errand for later and explain why.

Everyday Situations.prompt: You've had a minor but persistent health problem for weeks. You can get a faster private appointment that costs more, or a free public one with a long wait. Decide what you'll do and explain your reasoning.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Base your decision on how the problem is affecting your daily life, not just the cost.

Everyday Situations.prompt: You're deciding whether to fix your old washing machine or buy a new one. Make a decision and justify it.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Mention cost and at least one other factor.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Your work schedule changed and now clashes with picking up your kids from school. Propose a compromise to your manager and explain why it could work for both sides.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Your compromise must address both your needs and the company's.

Everyday Situations.prompt: A family member is choosing between two doctors — one available sooner but further away, one closer but with a longer wait. Recommend an option and explain your reasoning.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Base your recommendation on urgency, not just distance.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Your monthly subscription costs are adding up. Decide which one to cancel and explain your reasoning.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Choose only one subscription to cancel.

Everyday Situations.prompt: A friend has been invited to a wedding abroad but says the trip would be expensive. They ask what you think they should do. Recommend a decision and explain your reasoning.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Your recommendation must balance cost against the value of the relationship.

Everyday Situations.prompt: You're moving to a new city and must choose between two neighborhoods — one convenient but noisy, one quiet but far from work. Decide and justify it.
Everyday Situations.constraint: You must weigh convenience against quality of life.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Your team at work needs to choose a time for a weekly meeting that suits everyone's different schedules. Propose a solution and explain your reasoning.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Mention at least one compromise.

Everyday Situations.prompt: You're comparing two jobs: one pays slightly more with a long commute, one pays less but is close to home. Evaluate the pros and cons of each, then explain which matters more to you.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Weigh at least two factors for each job before reaching a conclusion.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Your family is choosing between two good schools for your child. Prioritise the factors that matter most — distance, reputation, cost, facilities — and explain which one wins.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Rank at least three factors before naming your final choice.

Everyday Situations.prompt: You've been offered a slightly better-paid job in a different city, but taking it means leaving close friends and family behind. Decide what you'll do and explain your reasoning.
Everyday Situations.constraint: You must weigh the relationship cost against the professional opportunity, not just the money.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Your internet stopped working and the company says a technician can't come for five days. Decide how you'll manage and explain your plan.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Mention at least one practical workaround.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Your phone broke and you're deciding what matters most in a replacement: price, reliability, or how fast you can get one. Prioritise your needs and explain your final choice.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Rank your priorities before stating your decision.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Two friends both want you to help them move house on the same weekend. Decide how you'll handle it and explain your reasoning.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Your answer must address both friendships.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Your building is voting on whether to install a new elevator, which will raise everyone's monthly fees. Decide how you'll vote and explain why.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Mention both the benefit and the cost.

Everyday Situations.prompt: You're deciding between cooking at home or eating out more often, based on your recent schedule and budget. Make a decision and justify it.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Support your decision with a specific reason from your daily life.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Your gym membership is expensive and you haven't been going often. Decide what to do and explain your reasoning.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Choose one specific action, not just 'I should think about it.'

Everyday Situations.prompt: A neighbor is choosing between two contractors to renovate their kitchen — one cheaper with a longer wait, one pricier but available now. They ask for your recommendation. Recommend one and explain your reasoning.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Your recommendation must address both time and money.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Your relative wants to stay with you for two weeks, but your apartment is small and you work from home. Decide how you'll handle it and explain your reasoning.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Your answer must consider both hospitality and practicality.

Everyday Situations.prompt: You're deciding whether to take public transport or buy a car based on your daily needs. Make a decision and justify it.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Mention at least one cost and one convenience factor.

Everyday Situations.prompt: Your local council is asking residents to choose between repairing the roads or improving the park. Decide how you'd vote and explain your reasoning.
Everyday Situations.constraint: Your answer must consider the needs of the wider community, not just yourself.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: You booked a hotel room online but arrive to find it's already occupied. Negotiate a solution with the front desk staff, considering you have nowhere else to stay tonight.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student negotiates a workable solution and gives at least one reason to support their preferred outcome.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Your neighbour's music has been too loud for the past three nights and you have an early start tomorrow. Talk to them and agree on a reasonable compromise.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student raises the issue politely and reaches a compromise using softened disagreement language.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: You and a colleague both want to take the same week off work. Discuss your reasons and try to reach a fair agreement.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student explains their reasons and works toward a fair agreement, acknowledging the colleague's position.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: A repair shop wants to charge more than the original quote to fix your laptop. Negotiate the price, explaining what you can realistically afford.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student states the discrepancy, negotiates a new price, and justifies their budget limit.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: A furniture shop sent you a sofa in the wrong colour and now claims it was your mistake when ordering online. Explain clearly why you believe the error was theirs and what you expect them to do about it.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student explains their position clearly, states evidence for their view, and states a desired outcome.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Your gym membership renewed automatically but you want to switch to a cheaper plan. Persuade the staff member to make the change without a penalty fee.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student persuades the staff member using at least one polite persuasion phrase and a clear reason.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: A friend wants to split a restaurant bill equally, but you only ordered a small dish while they ordered several courses. Discuss a fair way to split it.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student proposes a fair alternative and reaches agreement with the friend.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: You're sharing an apartment and one roommate keeps leaving dishes for days. Raise the issue and agree on a new system that works for both of you.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student resolves the conflict calmly and agrees on a concrete new system.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: You need to change a dentist appointment, but the only free slot clashes with an important work meeting. Persuade the receptionist to find another solution for you.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student persuades the receptionist to offer an alternative, giving a clear reason for the request.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: A delivery driver left your package with a neighbour without telling you, and it's now missing. Discuss the situation with the neighbour and decide what to do next.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student resolves the conflict calmly and agrees on a next step with the neighbour.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: You want a refund for a concert ticket because the event was postponed to a date you can't attend. Convince the box office to help you.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student persuades the box office using a clear reason and at least one persuasive phrase.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Two friends are planning a weekend trip but disagree about the budget. Work together to find a plan that suits you both.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student proposes options and reaches agreement that addresses both budgets.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Your landlord wants to raise the rent, but you feel the increase is too high given the apartment's condition. Discuss and try to reach a compromise.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student negotiates the increase and justifies their position with a specific reason.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: A colleague keeps taking credit for your ideas in meetings. Have a calm conversation with them about how you'd like things to change going forward.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student explains their position clearly and states what change they would like to see.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: You want to return a jacket that no longer fits, but you've lost the receipt. Persuade the shop assistant to help you anyway.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student persuades the shop assistant using a polite, reasoned argument.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: You and a friend are choosing a restaurant for a group dinner, but you have very different budgets. Find an option you can both agree on.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student proposes a compromise option and reaches agreement with the friend.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Your internet keeps cutting out, but the provider insists the problem is with your equipment, not their service. Resolve the disagreement and agree on how it will be fixed.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student resolves the conflict by presenting their view and agreeing on next steps with the provider.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Your tutor has raised their lesson price with very little notice. Explain your position on whether the increase feels fair and how you'd like to move forward.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student explains their position clearly and states a preferred way forward.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Your car mechanic recommends several repairs for your car, but you suspect not all of them are necessary. Persuade them to explain clearly which repairs are truly essential.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student persuades the mechanic to justify each recommendation, using at least one probing question.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: You and a family member disagree about which venue to book for a celebration. Talk it through and reach a decision everyone can accept.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student proposes reasons for their preference and reaches a joint decision.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: A shop refuses to exchange a gift because it was bought during a sale. Explain your situation and try to find a solution.
Simple Roleplay.constraint: Student persuades the shop assistant with a clear explanation and a suggested solution.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Your flight was delayed and you missed your connecting train, but airline staff say it isn't their responsibility. Resolve the disagreement and find out what they're willing to do.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: You want to cancel your phone contract early, but the company wants to charge a high cancellation fee. Explain your position on why the fee feels unfair and hear what they propose instead.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: A colleague wants to borrow money from you, but you're not comfortable lending the full amount. Discuss the situation honestly and agree on a solution.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: You're sharing a taxi with a stranger heading in a similar direction, but your destinations aren't identical. Agree on a fair route and how to split the fare.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Your child's school wants to charge an extra fee for a trip you feel is too expensive. Speak with a staff member about your concerns.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: A friend cancelled plans with you last minute for the second time. Have an honest conversation about how this affects your friendship.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: You want to negotiate working from home two days a week, but your manager prefers everyone in the office. Present your case and try to find a compromise.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Your energy bill was unexpectedly high this month, and you and the provider disagree about the cause. Work together to reach an agreement on how to resolve it.

Simple Roleplay.prompt: Two neighbours disagree about who should pay for a shared fence that needs repairing. Discuss the situation and agree on a fair arrangement.
